traced_rule: An input is traced when the flight's own record states it: here RocketPy's example notebook, which holds the team's inputs. What no RocketPy example records is a placeholder in the designs built from them, the seven compared flights' too, and doesn't count against the tag: the surface finish, the rail buttons' size, the fins' thickness where no airfoil file gives it, and their edge shape where no airfoil file or published section does. They move the drag, so a traced flight's inputs are stated, not exact. A flight is tagged not traced when its record leaves out, or contradicts, something else that moves the apogee.

design_file_traced_rule: For a flight read from a design file, the record is that file and its repository's page about the flight. The file states the rocket and names the motor. A stored simulation's launch conditions are what a simulation was run with, not a record of the day, so the site, the air, the wind and the rod count as not traced unless the page states them. So does the mass, unless the page says the rocket was weighed as flown, and the motor's curve where the reader warns that its file and its certifier's record disagree.

design_file_flights.title: Macie XL, flight 1 (AeroTech I284W)
design_file_flights.source: macie/index.md (the two flights; the file names that pair `maciexl-1-or` with flight 1) and macie/macie-xl.ork, read whole as OpenRocket 24.12 saved it
design_file_flights.motor_source: the stored simulation's motor configuration in macie/macie-xl.ork, which names the motor and the digest of its curve; the bundled ThrustCurve.org file that digest names is flown
design_file_flights.mass_source: macie/macie-xl.ork: its parts and the stage's mass and center overrides, which add to the parts as OpenRocket 24.12 weighs them; the motor's masses are the bundled catalog's for the motor, 313.6 g of propellant and 555.52 g loaded
design_file_flights.conditions_source: the stored simulation's launch conditions in macie/macie-xl.ork
design_file_flights.atmosphere: the 1976 US Standard Atmosphere, for the stored simulation's `isa`
design_file_flights.reference_rule: the apogee the altimeter worked out, in the log's header (its `Apogee:` line, in feet above the pad, 0.3048 m to the foot), which leaves out the ejection spike among the samples; never the highest sample
design_file_flights.altimeter_evidence: the log's first line names a PerfectFlite altimeter, `PerfectFlite SLCF`, and a PerfectFlite has a barometer and no accelerometer (docs/format/pf2.md)
untraced: no record gives the day, its air and wind, or the rail, and of the site only each log's header gives the pad's height above sea level (12 ft for flight 1, 37 ft for flight 2): the stored simulation's are flown, its sea level among them, and all nine simulations in the file carry the same ones
no record says the rocket was weighed as flown: the file's parts and overrides are flown

the reader warns that the motor's curve file disagrees with ThrustCurve.org's record of the motor (the figures are in the flight's `reader_warnings` in the JSON); the file the design's digest names is flown

the motor flies the bundled catalog's masses for it, 313.6 g of propellant and 555.52 g loaded, as every catalog motor does, where the curve file the design's digest names, and OpenRocket's own record of that digest, give 310.016 g and 555.072 g (the table's `mass_difference`)
reader_warnings: openrocket/rocket/stage[0]/bodytube[5]/innertube[3]: I284W's curve file 5f4294d20002e9000000003b is more than 1% from ThrustCurve.org's figures for it: total impulse -1.28%, average thrust +7.89%
design_file_flights.note: the stored simulation's wind carries a turbulence of a tenth of its speed, which is not flown: the wind here is steady. The parachutes are not flown either; the file opens the first at apogee, so neither moves it
